subject: Recap + proposed dedicated config: token mix, TPS, GPU ask
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Rajat Singh <rajat@edgecommerce.com>, Priya Menon <priya.m@edgecommerce.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 16:14:00 -0700
Subject: Quick recap + a couple follow-ups on dedicated sizing

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation about where EdgeCommerce is headed. Quick recap and concrete asks so we can move to a sizing proposal for Dedicated capacity.

Summary of needs (from call)
- Primary workload: conversational shopping assistant + product summarization + batch reranks for recommendations.
- Peak traffic: expected 1,200 QPS at peak for short-chat requests, with an 8:1 short-to-long request ratio.
- Token mix: short chats ~40 tokens on average; long summarization ~1,200 tokens average; batch reranks are smaller but run as multi-item calls.
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 220ms for short chats; longer requests can be up to 1.5s.
- Data requirement: customer PII restricted, possible requirement for VPC/private control plane later in the year.

Clarifying questions / asks (what we need from your side)
1) Can you share the sample traffic CSV you mentioned (timestamp, endpoint, tokens_in, tokens_out, qps_bucket)? Attached one we captured during the demo is great.
2) For the peak 1,200 QPS estimate — is that sustained over >10 minutes or bursty (seconds)? If bursty, any burst window numbers?
3) Do you have an internal expectation for concurrency per user session (e.g., multiple parallel requests per user)?

Early sizing direction (what we're considering)
- Model family: recommending a 2-step approach: H100-based pool for heavy short-chat throughput + A100/8GB-quantized pool for cost-sensitive batch reranks.
- Tentative Dedicated footprint: 4 x H100-80GB (for low-latency chat, high concurrency) + 2 x A100-40GB quantized nodes for reranks and background jobs. This hedges cost while giving headroom for KV cache memory.
- Autoscaling: reserve steady 60% of the pool with burst to 100% using a queued prewarm policy.

Next steps
- Rajat/Priya: drop the CSV to this thread (edge_traffic_sample_qps.csv) and confirm burst window behavior.
- Marissa/Aditya: if you agree, I’ll draft a micro-architecture and a perf-test plan (7-day run with traffic replay) and a cost estimate.

Attachments: edge_traffic_sample_qps.csv (csv), initial_sla_and_terms_draft.pdf (pdf)

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

From: Rajat Singh <rajat@edgecommerce.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 18:02:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + a couple follow-ups on dedicated sizing

Thanks Hannah — this is helpful. Dropping the CSV you requested (attached). A few clarifications inline:
- The 1,200 QPS is a peak sustained over ~15 minutes during sale events; we see very short microbursts up to ~1,800 QPS for 30-60s.
- Concurrency: typical session triggers 1-2 parallel calls, but bots can fan-out to 4 in some flows.
- For the KV/cache: we need to preserve short-term session context for up to 30 minutes per user; memory matters.

Also, about private deployments — we are not ready for on-prem yet but need VPC/private control plane and KMS integration.

Attached: edge_traffic_sample_qps.csv

—Rajat

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 08:07:12 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Quick recap + proposed dedicated config — notes for perf team

Forwarding Rajat's CSV and Hannah's recap to start drafting perf test matrix. Initial thoughts:
- Given 15-minute sustained peak and 30-60s microbursts, we should size for steady-state 1,200 QPS and have headroom for 1.5x bursts via burst pool.
- Token mix skew: because long requests consume large tokens, cost model must track token-weighted concurrency. Recommend we simulate both: (a) 85% short chat traffic replay and (b) 15% long summarization heavy requests.
- Batch sizing: use per-request batching for reranks (up to batch size 64) with quantized A100 pool to save cost.

Proposed perf run (I'll prep details): 7-day replay with:
- 24h warmup (to populate KV cache)
- 72h steady-state at 1,200 QPS
- 48h timed bursts replay (simulate microburst windows)
- Capture: p95/p99 latency, GPU utilization, token throughput, cold-start times, memory pressure for KV cache

I'll draft a tentative resource matrix. Aditya — can you weigh in on the H100 vs A100 split and any scheduling recommendations?

-Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rajat Singh <rajat@edgecommerce.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:22:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick recap + proposed dedicated config — notes for perf team

Thanks — quick technical reaction and a proposed starting config we can iterate on.

Technical reactions
- H100s are the right choice for short-chat 95th latency SLOs at that QPS and concurrency because of FP16 throughput and larger HBW; they also give more KV cache headroom with bigger VRAM.
- A100 quantized nodes are good for reranks and background work; they lower cost per token for long sequence workloads if we use GPTQ-style quantization and int8 kernels.

Proposed starting Dedicated footprint (for perf-run and initial contract):
- Primary pool (low-latency chat): 4 x H100-80GB (pinned to the short-chat model variant), each node exposed via 16 serving workers, continuous batching tuned to 8-12ms latency windows.
- Secondary pool (batch/long): 2 x A100-40GB quantized nodes, with larger batch windows and lower concurrency per-worker.
- Routing rules: route 95% of short-chat traffic to H100 pool; heavy summarization and reranks to A100 pool. Overflow policy: when H100 saturated, fallback to an autoscaled burst pool (same gen) with degraded latency SLO flagged.

Perf-test targets
- Achieve sustained 1,200 QPS with p95 <= 220ms on short-chat replay.
- Handle 1.5x microbursts (1,800 QPS) for 60s with p95 degradation under 2x baseline but no errors.

Next operational asks
1) Rajat — confirm CSV fields matched and share any unusually large sequences for sampling.
2) Hannah/Marissa — I'll prepare a node-by-node cost estimate (hourly + estimated monthly) and a draft canary rollout plan (gradual traffic ramp + automated fallback).

I’ll attach the perf-run checklist to the drive link once I’ve sketched it.

-Aditya
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
